summary: A scholarship for mid-career professionals from eligible developing countries, run by the World Bank Group with funding from the Government of Japan. It supports a master's degree in a development-related field at one of the participating programmes, 44 programmes at 24 universities according to the World Bank. You must already hold an unconditional admission offer and have at least three years of paid development-related work.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a national of a country on the 2027 eligible list (Annex 1 of the guidelines) and not a dual citizen of any developed country. Nationality rules are strict and the form has no way to apply for a country that is not on the list.

You must hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) earned at least three years before the application deadline. At the time you apply you must be working full time in a paid development-related job, and you must have at least three years of paid development-related employment since your first degree, gained within the six years before the deadline. Part-time paid work can count if you state the share of time worked. Paid development-related internships count. Time spent in graduate study, mandatory national or military service, unpaid work and volunteering do not count, except that nationals of countries on the fragile and conflict-affected list (Annex 3) may use unpaid or informal development work and the Secretariat takes the limited local job market into account. Work in an unregistered business or without a contract does not count for other applicants.

On or before the deadline you must have been admitted unconditionally (except for funding, and a medical certificate) for the coming academic year to a participating master's programme in a country that is neither your country of citizenship nor your country of residence. Double or dual degrees with a participating programme are not accepted. If you are admitted to more than one participating programme you must choose one before applying, and the scholarship cannot be moved to another programme later.

You are not eligible if you are an Executive Director, an alternate or any type of staff (including consultants and temporary staff) of the World Bank Group, or a close relative of one (mother, father, sister, half-sister, brother, half-brother, son, daughter, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew). Anyone currently studying in a participating programme is not eligible, and neither is anyone who was offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship before and declined it or left without graduating. Applicants must be in good health (stated on the programme page).

There is no age limit. Having an earlier master's degree, or earlier Government of Japan funding, does not exclude you. The Secretariat does not give opinions on individual eligibility or on whether an admission letter is unconditional, and it makes no exceptions to the criteria. A separate application route for Japanese nationals exists and is not covered here.
age_experience_notes: No minimum or maximum age. Required experience: at least three years of paid development-related employment since the bachelor's degree, within the six years before the deadline, and a full-time paid development-related job when you apply.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays for tuition for the master's programme, basic medical insurance arranged by the university, a monthly allowance for on-campus living costs (accommodation, food and books; the amount depends on the host country), and economy-class return airfare at the start and end of the programme plus US$600 for each trip. It covers the length of the programme or two years, whichever is shorter. The World Bank does not tell applicants the total value, because it depends on the length and location of the programme. The scholarship is described as a supplement to other funding, and you must send the Secretariat documents about any other awards you hold.
programmes_note: Only master's programmes on the World Bank's participating-programmes lists qualify; the programme name must be on the list. Window 1 has 8 universities and 11 programmes, and Window 2 has 16 universities and 32 programme entries on the lists I read. Programmes cover development-related fields such as economic and public policy, public health, development practice, taxation, infrastructure management, water, climate and urban change. The scholarship does not support PhD or undergraduate study, distance learning, short courses, conferences, thesis writing or research projects.
institutions_note: Window 1: Brandeis University (Heller School), Columbia University (SIPA), Johns Hopkins University (Bloomberg School of Public Health), KIT Royal Tropical Institute with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of California Berkeley (Goldman School of Public Policy), University of Tsukuba, Williams College (Center for Development Economics), Yale University (School of Management). Window 2: Australian National University (Crawford School), Columbia University (SIPA), Erasmus University (IHS Rotterdam and IISS The Hague), IHE Delft, Keio University, London School of Economics, GRIPS, Saitama University, SOAS University of London, Stanford University, Universite Clermont-Auvergne (FERDI), University of Leeds, University of Oxford, University of Tokyo (Agriculture and Life Science; Graduate School of Public Policy), Yokohama National University. You apply to the window under which your programme is listed, and you may submit only one application. Only programmes shortlisted by the university will receive the link to the application form.

summary.detail: Master's degree in a development-related field at a participating programme, 2027-28 academic year. Funding lasts for the programme length or two years, whichever is shorter. Window 1 programmes take applications from 18 January to 26 February 2027; Window 2 programmes from 29 March to 21 May 2027. The teaching language is set by each programme and is not stated on the lists.

benefits.conditions: For the length of the programme or two years, whichever is shorter. The total value is not published; it depends on programme length and location.

benefits.limit_text: Basic medical insurance arranged by the university
Monthly allowance for on-campus living costs including accommodation, food and books; amount varies by host country
benefits.conditions: Amount not stated on the pages read.

benefits.limit_text: Economy round-trip airfare at the start and end of the programme, plus a US$600 travel allowance per trip
benefits.conditions: Between the home country and the host university. Scholars admitted to a US university must travel on a J-1 visa or the scholarship is withdrawn.

benefits.limit_text: Visa costs; family members' costs; extracurricular courses; credits beyond the degree minimum; language training not offered by the programme; extra travel; research, materials, field trips, workshops, internships; equipment such as computers; resident permit fees
benefits.conditions: The university deposit to hold a place is also the student's responsibility.

requirements.text: One online application form, completed in English or the language of the master's programme, including the signature page agreement (type your name; no scanned signature). Use a computer, not a phone. Submitting more than one application, or sending any part by post, email, fax or in person, leads to disqualification.

Two professional recommendations, submitted online by the recommenders in English, from people who saw your paid development-related work first-hand. Exactly two are allowed. Recommendations from professors based on your time as a student do not count. You must send the recommendation request form before you submit the application and must not draft the letters yourself.

Proof of the years of recent development-related work: an employer letter on letterhead, signed, dated within three months before the deadline for current employment, stating start date and title; similar letters with start and end dates for earlier jobs; for self-employment, a government registration document.
requirements.conditional_rule: Nationals of fragile and conflict-affected countries upload employment proof where they have it and explain in a document if they cannot

requirements.text: Scanned diploma of your bachelor's degree and, if you have one, your most advanced graduate degree. A transcript is not accepted instead unless it clearly shows the degree and graduation date. Do not upload additional transcripts or GPA records.

CV in the World Bank format (Annex 4: employment record since the bachelor's degree, key responsibilities, most important accomplishment; optional sections for other information and education). Paid work only in the employment record; unpaid work goes under a Volunteer Work heading. Annex 4 format is suggested in the FAQ and listed as required in the guidelines.

Letter of admission, unconditional except for financing, for the coming academic year to the participating master's programme you want funded, located outside your country of citizenship and residence. Conditions about visas, first-year grades or deposits do not make it conditional; conditions about missing documents or language scores do.
English translations of any document not in English; upload both the original and the translation. A certified translation is not required.

Scanned passport identification page, with a name identical to the application form, within three business days of the scholarship offer. If you have no valid passport, a birth or marriage certificate is accepted.
Health certificate from a medical doctor stating you are in good health to travel and study, less than three months old at the programme start, sent at least 21 days before you travel.

application_steps.title: Get unconditional admission to a participating programme
application_steps.detail: Apply to a participating master's programme and obtain an admission letter that is unconditional except for funding. Check which window your programme is in. The Secretariat does not rule on individual eligibility or admission letters. Pay any university deposit yourself.

application_steps.title: Get shortlisted by the university and receive the form link
application_steps.detail: The university decides whether you meet the admission and eligibility requirements. Only applicants a programme has shortlisted receive the link to the online application form, so contact the programme to confirm. You may draft the form but must not submit it before uploading the unconditional admission letter.

application_steps.title: Send two recommendation requests early
application_steps.detail: Name two professional recommenders in the recommendation request form before you submit the application. Each gets a unique email link; ask them to check spam folders. If both recommendations are not in by the deadline, the application is not reviewed.

application_steps.title: Submit one application in the right window
application_steps.detail: Window 1 runs 18 January to 26 February 2027 and Window 2 runs 29 March to 21 May 2027 (the Window 2 guidelines give 12:00 noon EST on 21 May). Apply only under the window where your programme is listed, for one programme only. The Secretariat advises submitting at least a week before the deadline and does not promise answers to emails sent in the last three business days.

application_steps.title: Two assessors score each eligible application
application_steps.detail: Two independent assessors score each eligible application from 1 to 10. Weights: professional experience 30%, professional recommendations 30%, commitment to the home country 30%, educational background 10%. Incomplete or ineligible applications are not reviewed.

application_steps.title: Secretariat review and Steering Committee approval
application_steps.detail: The average score is combined with geographic distribution, gender balance, unusual circumstances or hardship, and limited access to financial resources. The Secretariat sends finalists to the Steering Committee, made up of World Bank Board members and management. Winners are notified after approval; the Window 1 FAQ says successful applicants will likely hear by the end of March 2027, and unsuccessful applicants are also notified.

application_steps.title: Send ID and health certificate on time
application_steps.detail: Finalists send a passport identification page within three business days of the offer and a doctor's health certificate at least 21 days before travel. Missing either on time means disqualification.

application_steps.title: Travel, study and return home
application_steps.detail: Scholars admitted to a US university must enter on a J-1 visa. The scholarship cannot be transferred to another programme. The programme page says scholars commit to return home after graduating to contribute to their country's development. Tell the Secretariat about any other awards you hold.

not_stated: The total value of the scholarship and the monthly allowance amount (the FAQ says the Secretariat does not give these to applicants)
The teaching language and length of each participating programme (not on the lists)
The notification date for Window 2 applicants (the Window 2 documents still carry 2025 dates)
A detailed statement of the return-home obligation (the programme page says only that scholars commit to return)

notes: The Window 2 guidelines contain old dates ('June 2025', 'mid-July 2025') copied from an earlier year, so I did not use them as notification dates.

Window 2 programme list has 32 entries across 16 universities; Window 1 has 11 across 8. The World Bank page says 44 programmes at 24 universities, so the page totals differ slightly from the lists. Only the first 25 programmes (all of Window 1, then the first Window 2 entries) are included; the rest are on the catalogue page. Remaining Window 2 programmes include: GRIPS Tax Course; Saitama University; SOAS (Development Economics, Economics); Stanford Master in International Policy; Clermont-Auvergne/FERDI; Leeds (four programmes); Oxford (three); University of Tokyo (two); Yokohama National University (two).
The programme page for Keio University links to the IHE Delft page, which may be a link error on the World Bank site.
The Annex 1 list contains Kosovo, which is not in the stored nationality list; the stored list may need checking against Annex 1 for the 2027 call.
Stored milestone 'Window 2 deadline 21 May 2027' is confirmed; the Window 1 deadline is 26 February 2027.
